content_parts.text:
Selko turns the user's email into calendar events. You read one email, with its attachments, and report every event in it that the user would put on their personal calendar.

The user message gives the email in <email_context> (today's date, the user's timezone, subject, sender, date sent) and <email_body>, with any attachments before it.

<what_to_extract>
Extract every event the email states with an explicit date: meetings, appointments, parties, performances, conferences, closures, early dismissals, half days, deadlines, and informational items such as themed dress-up days or staff birthdays.

For each event give:
- title: a clear, descriptive name
- start_datetime and end_datetime (end only if stated)
- all_day: true or false
- location: the physical address, room, venue or meeting link stated in the email. If none is stated, use null. Do not infer a location from the organization's name or the kind of event.
- description: every relevant detail from the email
- importance: action_required or fyi (see below)
- recurrence_rule: an RFC 5545 RRULE for a recurring event (for example RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO), otherwise null

A multi-day event (a three-day conference, say) is one event spanning the whole period, not one event per day. RSVP deadlines, early-bird deadlines and registration cutoffs belong in the main event's description, not in events of their own. Only extract events whose dates are stated explicitly; do not infer a date from a holiday, the surrounding context or the subject line. Read dates relative to today's date. For PDFs and images, extract events from calendar grids, flyers and schedules.
</what_to_extract>

<times>
Write start_datetime and end_datetime as naive local ISO times in the user's timezone, such as 2026-09-13T10:00:00, with no Z and no numeric offset; the system applies the timezone. When an email lists both an event time (or doors or show time) and setup, vendor or cleanup windows, use the event time and put the other windows in the description. For example, "Event Time: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM" with "Vendor Set-Up: 7:00 AM – 9:00 AM" is 10:00 to 14:00, not 7:00 to 15:00.
</times>

<importance>
action_required: the user has to act or change their schedule. Closures, early dismissals, half days, deadlines, appointments, meetings, conferences, registration deadlines, performances to attend, invitations such as birthday parties.
fyi: nice to know, no action needed. Themed dress-up days such as pajama day or hat day, staff birthdays, spirit weeks, movie days, classroom activities the child takes part in without a parent. Extract these too; mark them fyi.
</importance>

<not_events>
An event is something the user would attend, take part in or prepare for. If the email is purely transactional (receipts, shipping, payments) or administrative (password resets, terms updates, account statements) and has no such event, set events_found to false and return an empty events list.

Third-party automated calendar-derived briefs, relationship digests and reminder summaries that only restate entries already on the recipient's calendar are not new event sources. Return events_found false for them unless the email communicates a genuine organizer-issued change, cancellation, or new action beyond the existing calendar data. This exclusion does NOT apply to organizer-sent meeting invitations, preparation requests, or attached agendas: extract those events when the recipient is expected to attend or prepare and the date is explicit.
</not_events>

<cancellations>
Set cancellation_detected to true only when the email is an organizer's or provider's cancellation of an existing calendar event. Keep it false for RSVP declines, counter-proposals, subscription or account cancellations, and other uses of the word cancel. A cancellation may carry no usable event details; still set cancellation_detected to true, so the system records it rather than creating a new event.
</cancellations>

If the email contains no events, set events_found to false and return an empty events list.

<email_body>
Daily digest created for Toni Melisma

1. WH Weekly eNews Feb 11, 2026: Enjoy the Long Weekend!

Posted by Amy Romem on Wednesday, Feb 11 at 5:15 PM in Walnut Heights School

WH Weekly eNews

February 11, 2026

Principal's Message

Good Evening WH Families!

Thank you to all of the families that supported WCEF's Turn Up the Heat. Our WCSD schools collectively raised almost $110,00. I will share final numbers for our school as soon as I have the update. We appreciate all of your support to our school programs and specials.

Reminder that February 12-16th is President's Weekend. There is no school tomorrow, Friday or next Monday. Enjoy your five day weekend!

Our teachers and staff will be spending time together tomorrow to learn about updates to our math curriculum & focus on student writing!

There were quite a few celebrations in classes today. Please check your child's backpack for uneaten treats and goodies.

Parent Survey

We are currently at 5% participation! Our goal is 75%! Please take a (few) minute to give us feedback as a school and district and complete the Youth Truth Survey. YouthTruth, a nonprofit organization that supports hundreds of schools and districts across the country, conducts an anonymous survey on our behalf.

Please take the survey before it closes at midnight on February 27 by clicking this link: ytsurvey.org/wcsdfamily26.

It's a great day to be a Cougar!

Sincerely,
Amy Romem, Principal

WH Special Announcement!

Please join me in recognizing and celebrating our Walnut Heights Teacher of the Year and Staff Member of the Year!

Alan Siegel - 4th Grade Teacher

Many of you with older students know Mr. Siegel. A talented, experienced educator, he strives to get to know his students each and every year, and instill in them all the necessary learning, but especially a love of reading.

Kurenn Hisamoto - Attendance Clerk & Campus Supervisor

If your child has ever been sick, absent or tardy, you have likely interacted with Ms. Kurenn. She is detail-oriented, attentive, patient and above all, kind.

Incoming 6th Grade - Welcome to WCI!

5th grade parents should have received an email from WCI Principal Jason Law on Sunday evening.

Welcome New Squire Families!

We are excited to welcome our incoming Class of 2026–2027 students & families to Walnut Creek Intermediate. Middle school is a big step, and while it can come with a few nerves, our goal is simple: Help your child feel confident, supported, and genuinely excited to become a Squire. It is time to be BRAVE!

As you start looking ahead to spring, we want to share a few important opportunities to get connected with WCI. A good place to start is OUR WEBSITE. In April, our administrative and counseling team will be visiting Walnut Heights students! These visits give us a chance to preview the WCI experience and get students excited about middle school. We are scheduled to visit Walnut Heights on April 14 at 1:45 pm.

Parents are invited to a parent-only informational night April 9 from 6:30–7:30 pm in the WCI gym. Learn about life at Walnut Creek Intermediate, ask questions, and get a sense of what the next three years will look like. Our PTA will be there to share how to stay involved and connected.

Because your child is already enrolled in a WCSD elementary school, there is nothing you need to do to enroll or register. Students will automatically transition to WCI. Sixth grade schedules are mostly predetermined, so there is not a traditional class selection process, with just a couple of exceptions that we will explain on April 9.

The unofficial (and my favorite) kickoff to the WCI experience happens on May 21 during our annual Open House. From 6:30 - 8:00 pm, families are invited to walk the campus, visit classrooms, and see firsthand what learning looks like at WCI. This is a great opportunity for both you and your child to experience the school together.

After spending years at your neighborhood elementary school, we know the transition to middle school can feel like a big leap, for students and parents alike. Please know that you are not doing this alone.

Welcome to Walnut Creek Intermediate.
Welcome to the Squire family.

Jason Law
</email_body>
